record.original_question: Let M be the one-dimensional centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, and let BV(R) denote the Banach space of functions f : R -> R of bounded total variation with norm ||f||_{BV(R)} = |f(-infinity)| + Var(f). Is the map M : BV(R) -> BV(R) continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ denote the one-dimensional centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator, defined for a locally integrable function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ by
$$Mf(x) \;=\; \sup_{r>0}\,\frac{1}{2r}\int_{x-r}^{x+r}|f(t)|\,dt.$$
Let $\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Banach space of functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ of bounded total variation, equipped with the norm
$$\|f\|_{\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})} \;=\; |f(-\infty)| + \mathrm{Var}(f),$$
where $f(-\infty) = \lim_{x\to-\infty} f(x)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(f)$ is the total variation of $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$. It is known that $M$ maps $\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$ into itself.

Determine whether the map $M:\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})\to\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$ is continuous.
artifact.status_search_result: The continuity of the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator on BV(ℝ) appears to remain open. The analogous question for the uncentered maximal operator on BV(ℝ) has been resolved affirmatively (González-Riquelme, 2021). For the centered operator, partial progress is known: Kurka established BV-boundedness, and recent work (González-Riquelme–Madrid, 2023) proved continuity of f ↦ (Mf)′ from W^{1,1}(ℝ) to L^1(ℝ), but full BV(ℝ)→BV(ℝ) continuity for the centered operator does not appear to have been established.

status_evidence.title: BV continuity for the uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator
status_evidence.snippet: The continuity of the map f↦M˜f from BV(R) to itself has been proved for the uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator. The only open problems in this program are related to the centered case.
status_evidence.claim: BV-continuity is solved for the uncentered case; the centered case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Continuity for the one-dimensional centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator at the derivative level
status_evidence.snippet: Continuity of f ↦ (Mf)' from W^{1,1}(R) to L^1(R) is proved for the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on the centered operator has been made at the derivative level on Sobolev spaces.
